name: House — wireframe
notes: A 10 × 7 m house (7 m over all, the garage's wall bands inside it) on a sloped parcel, its ground and first floors pushed 1 m out of the downhill face and the garage 3 m, the driveway cut into the hill and ramped down to the road.
The house is turned 8.06° about its south-east corner to lie parallel to the north-east boundary, 1 m off it (D6).
Heights are metres above the garage-floor datum: real 991.11 m a.s.l. is y 0. The parcel and relief come from the terrain app's survey.

Levels in a terrain profile are finished surfaces; a slab's top is that number, its underside `slab` below; a wall is `wall` thick on the hill side of the line it holds — except the garage's own bands, which lie inside the envelope (z 0–0.3 and 6.7–7) so the house is 7 m over all.

The garage is 6 m clear, x 5.7–11.7 (`x0` 5.7, `extendFront` 1.7), with a 0.30 front wall at x 11.7–12 carrying the 5.00 × 2.25 sectional-door opening under a lintel; the box sits 0.30 further into the hill than the earlier x 6–12 so the clear length and the 3.70 apron both hold. The back 2.7 m of the hill stay in place under the ground floor, so the pit is shallower there and the retaining walls behind it shorter. Inside, along the north wall: a 1.00 stair (z 0.3–1.3) with a railing on its open side, a 1.36 landing inside the door, 16 treads of 0.29 rising 17 × 0.171 to the hall at the back wall line (the 17th riser is the wall), storage under the back 2.25 of the flight, open to the garage, and 5.35 across for two slots (car 2.60 left, quad or second car 2.75 right). The ground and first floors are moved 1 m forward and shortened 2 m at the back, x 3–11, 8 m long (`x0` 3, `extendFront` 1), so the ground floor's slab covers the garage to x 11. A 2 m balcony at ground-floor level (`balcony`, x 11–13) stands in front of the ground floor: its first metre is the garage's roof, its second projects over the garage door. The envelope stays x 0–10: it is the frame the turn and the cut are measured from, not the house's outline.

The apron is what the cut leaves in front of the garage door, so it carries its own `ring` (model frame): the fillet's corner (13, 7), the outer wall, the cut's north edge back to the house face (8.87, −1), the face down to the house's north-east corner (9.02, 0.07), the garage's north edge to its corner (11, −0.21) and the garage's turned face to its south-east corner (11.98, 6.72). Recompute those four turned points if the turn or the garage's depth changes.

The yard south of the house is set out on the house's own frame, turned with it: its north edge is the house's south wall (house x 3–11 at z 7), its west and east edges run in line with the house's end walls (house x 3 and x 11) down to the parcel boundary, and the boundary closes it. The east edge reaches the boundary at x 12.54, inside the ramp's uphill wall at 12.7. It is cut down to the ground floor's 0 where the hill stands above it; where the ground lies below, no fill is planned yet — that is decided once the house is built (`fill: true` and a `taper` band on the east edge would add it). Recompute the ring (the four turned points) if the turn or the floors' extent changes.

The house from the plan page (projects/xhevo/house/plan.html, generated by scripts/xhevo-plan-to-scene.mjs): 12 × 7 outside, x 0 to 12, with the glass gable at the front over the garage and no balcony, under one roof (ids rf-*) that starts 3.00 over the ground floor at the side walls and rises at 0.7 per metre to 5.45 at the ridge, 0.40 past the sides and the back, 1.00 past the glass; the side walls stand to the eaves, the back wall and the glass are gables under it; behind the living room's back wall the outer walls start on the fill at 0.8, since there is no house under the bedrooms. Walls 0.30, partitions 0.10. The kitchen is an L in the yard corner, its back wall only as long as the kitchen. The garage flight's hole x 5.7 to 9.18 is closed by a lid on the flight's pitch (2.12 at the landing, down to the floor at x 9.18), one plane. The two bedrooms are half a level up at +1 over the hill end, x 0 to 4.9, on fill (ids gf-fill-*): the hill end is not dug, the soil is made up to 0.8 and their slab sits on it (ids hl-* for the bedrooms). 6 risers of 0.167 climb from the living room against its back wall in the middle of the house, 5 treads of 0.2, 1 long, the last riser being the landing's floor in the wall line; the landing faces two doors side by side, and through each the bedroom is straight ahead and its bath to the side, in the front corner on the outer wall; the wall between the bedrooms is on the centre line. The slab of the ground level still runs unbroken under the stair hole: levels have no holes.
